sources.note: No descriptive source on Lenyima surfaced in any of these indexes.

sources.citation: Spreda, Klaus & Janice Spreda. 1966. The phonological data of Agbo. Appendix IX in Kenneth L. Pike, Tagmemic and matrix linguistics applied to selected African languages (ERIC ED010547), Ann Arbor. [Legbo/Agbo, sister language, NOT Lenyima]
sources.note: For Agbo (Legbo), p.281: 'Stress is not phonemic. Two factors control the distribution of stress within the word: (1) Tone: the stress is born by the syllable with the highest tone. (2) Linear position in the word: out of several syllables with the same height of tone the one nearest to the end of the word bears the stress.' Not applicable to Lenyima; noted as nearest-relative statement only.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Adedamola Aregbesola & Thelma Araokanmi. 2023. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Legboic Languages of Cross River State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2023-001. SIL International. vi+54 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sect. 6.3 'Phonetic inventory' (pp.13-15) gives pooled consonant/7-vowel tables for Lenyima/Lekpeti/Legbo wordlists, 'tentative'; Appendix E p.36: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Tone-marked 222-item Lenyima wordlist. 'stress' 0 hits, 'accent' 0 hits. Sect. 4 states there has been 'very little direct data collection and documentation' and knows no phonology of Lenyima.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020 [Edition IV, text dated 2019]. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 198 pp. Entry 290 'Lenyima' (p.64-65 of the PDF text).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content: the Lenyima entry gives names, location and classification and lists no references, wordlist, grammar or literacy material at all (contrast entry 287 Legbo: Grammar Spreda & Spreda 1966, Bendor-Samuel & Spreda 1969, Hyman et al. 2002, Paster 2003, Hyman & Udoh 2006, Udoh 2007, Hyman 2009; Dictionary Udoh 2004; entry 292 Leyigha: 'Comparative: Blench (2016)' only). Confirms that Blench knows no descriptive source for Lenyima.

sources.citation: Faraclas, Nicholas. 1986. Cross River as a model for the evolution of Benue-Congo nominal class concord systems. Studies in African Linguistics 17(1): 40-54.
sources.note: Nothing on Lenyima. Family-level only, p.41: 'many Cross River languages exhibit very interesting and complex pitch systems in which basically two-level tone systems interact with accent or stress systems to establish conditions favorable to the phonemicization of a third level of contrastive tone.' No language-specific stress rule; no Legboic data.
